issues.body: `_invokes_command` checks `token in line.split()`, but shell quoting is removed before argv reaches Python. For example, `run: python3 scripts/account-usage.py "--persist-limits" usage.json` really invokes the persistence entrypoint, while `line.split()` produces the distinct token `"--persist-limits"`. A second workflow using that entirely ordinary spelling is therefore omitted from `_workflows_invoking`; `serialization_premise_errors` can still report that only dispatch.yml invokes persistence, and the new workflow proceeds because its own production-path premise check sees the same false result. The tests cover comments, prose, and a suffixed token, but no shell-equivalent quoted spelling.
issues.fix_hint: Tokenize executable shell text with a shell-aware lexer (and handle command separators/continuations consistently), then compare the decoded argv token. Add a synthetic second workflow that passes `"--persist-limits"` and assert both that it is enumerated and that `persist_limits` refuses before any `gh` call. Include single-quoted and separator-adjacent controls if those forms are supported by the reader.
issues.title: Quoted persist flags bypass workflow invocation discovery

verdict.summary: The production-path enforcement and body-write flag coverage address the prior blocker and one prior major, and prose/comments no longer satisfy the workflow scan. One soundness gap remains in the invocation reader: it models shell argv with whitespace splitting, so ordinary shell quoting can hide a real persistence invocation. Because that lets a second workflow enter the guarded read/edit path without being counted, the serialization premise can still return empty in the condition it is meant to refuse.
